name: River flooding – Bow and Elbow rivers (Calgary, Canmore)

geo.extent: Bow and Elbow river valleys from the Rockies to Calgary

description: Calgary lies at the confluence of the Bow and Elbow rivers, which flood from heavy rain on snowmelt in early summer; the 2013 flood is the reference event. The City publishes flood hazard maps dividing the flood hazard area into four risk categories (updated maps not yet adopted as of 2026-10-30).

documented_events: 2013 southern Alberta flood (details not verified from an official page in this record)
practical_implications: Check the City of Calgary flood map for any address

sources.title: Understand flooding – Flood maps and river flows
Canada's Changing Climate Report (2019) – Headline statements
sources.publisher: Government of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada, lead)
sources.methodology: Assessment report; statements are assessments of observed and projected change, not local forecasts

verification.notes: Event facts quoted or paraphrased from the cited official pages on 2026-10-30. Exposure and implications are agent-04 interpretation.

limitations: The 2013 event figures were not retrieved from an official source on 2026-10-30; no figures are stored. Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
